input.quote: 3.4 HDI's General Manager (as hereinafter defined), may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments during the Company's normal business hours. The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI.
input.rationale: Section 3.4 (p0022) is the only audit/inspection right in the Agreement that binds us; the confidentiality (§ 8) and General Manager (§ 5.4) provisions contain no further verification rights, and no other clause gives HDI access to our books or systems. As drafted the right is exercisable an unlimited number of times, which is walk-away territory under the rule ("Unlimited or unannounced audits"), so the clause fails the fallback on frequency. The other fallback elements are already satisfied or bettered: HDI must give 30 days' prior written notice (double the 15-day fallback and equal to the preferred), inspection is during our normal business hours, and HDI bears its own inspection fees unconditionally (better than the 10 %/5 % underpayment carve-outs). The inspection is limited to records relating to the payment calculation, so there is no system-access language to delete. We therefore make the single minimal change needed to reach the fallback — a once-per-year cap. Preferred-level refinements not pressed here (inspection by an independent, confidentiality-bound auditor rather than HDI's own General Manager, and an off-site-where-possible preference) are noted only; HDI is in any event bound by § 8.3 as to our confidential information.

proposal.summary: Cap HDI's records inspection right at once per year.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have capped HDI's inspection right at once per year, since as drafted it could be exercised without limit. The existing 30 days' prior written notice and HDI-borne inspection costs already meet our position, so we have left them unchanged.
